sentences.text: The snout of Pissarrachampsa was relatively short, making up about 70% of the total skull length, which is shorter than in other crocodyliforms.
A deep notch between the upper jaw bones allowed an enlarged fourth tooth in the lower jaw to fit when the mouth was closed.
Thick rims around the large triangular holes on the skull roof are a unique diagnostic feature of Pissarrachampsa.
Unlike other baurusuchids, the four small depressions at the back of the Pissarrachampsa skull are visible from the side view.
Pissarrachampsa had four Eustachian tube openings under the skull, with the outer pair being larger than the inner pair.
Pissarrachampsa likely laid small clutches of only 4 to 5 eggs and provided extensive parental care, a trait more common in modern mammals than crocodiles.
The name Pissarrachampsa means "sandstone crocodile" in reference to the local name of the sandstones where the fossils were found.
The genus Pissarrachampsa was described by Montefeltro, Larsson, and Langer in 2011.
Pissarrachampsa likely preyed on sauropods and other crocodylomorphs.
Pissarrachampsa was likely preyed upon by theropod dinosaurs including abelisaurids, carcharodontosaurids, and megaraptora.
A 2014 study confirmed that Pissarrachampsa belongs to the subfamily Pissarrachampsinae.
Fossils of Pissarrachampsa were found near Gurinhatã, Brazil, in the Late Cretaceous Vale do Rio do Peixe Formation.
Pissarrachampsa lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages.
